title: PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) Training Note: Low-Balance Alerts, Disconnect Warnings and Alert Settings
content:
**The rule.** On PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) a low-balance alert is sent when the prepaid balance falls below the account's low-balance alert amount, and again only after the tier's repeat interval in elapsed hours while it stays below. A disconnect warning alert is sent when the prepaid balance divided by the average daily charge projects the tier's disconnect warning days or fewer days remaining. The average daily charge is the total of the daily charge lines of the tier's projection history (the service days ending on the day before the current date, on the same prepay account) divided by the number of days in that history, rounded to the cent. Disconnected, reconnected, weather-hold and counseling referral alerts are sent when those events occur.

The member may change the low-balance alert amount to any amount from the tier's lowest through its highest alert amount, inclusive, and the alert channel to any of the tier's alert channels; an amount outside the range is not accepted and the previous setting stands. At enrollment the low-balance alert amount is the amount the member chooses within the range, or the tier's default alert amount when the member names none.

Alerts are courtesy notices: a failed delivery never delays a disconnection that is otherwise permitted, but a disconnect warning must have been sent.

### Questions answered

**When is a disconnect warning due?** Hypothetical figures on PrePay Power Residential (projection history of 7 days, warning at 3 days): daily charge lines of the 7 days ending yesterday total 22.40, so the average daily charge is 3.20; a balance of 9.50 projects 9.50 divided by 3.20, about 2.97 days, which is 3 or fewer, so the warning is sent. A balance of 9.70 projects about 3.03 days, so it is not.

**A member asks for an alert amount of 8.00 on PrePay Power Outbuilding.** The lowest amount on that tier is 10.00, so 8.00 is not accepted and the existing alert amount stands.

**A member asks for 100.00 on PrePay Power Residential.** That is the highest amount of the range, which is inclusive, so it is accepted.

**An alert text could not be delivered. Does the disconnection wait?** No. A failed delivery never delays a disconnection that is otherwise permitted, provided a disconnect warning was sent.

**The balance has stayed below the alert amount since a low-balance alert 10 hours ago.** A further low-balance alert waits until the repeat interval (24 elapsed hours on every tier) has passed while the balance stays below.
